name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 9 points on the partisan baseline
Jacqui Irwin holds a large fundraising edge with outside support and no opposition spending against her
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 95%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 9-point Democratic lean, Irwin's decisive money advantage, and markets pricing her near 95% all point to a comfortable hold despite Brownley's retirement. The open-seat nature and absence of polling justify trimming the expected margin slightly below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Gallucci or a top-two runoff matchup against a stronger Democrat could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Julia Brownley's retirement leaves this Ventura County-area seat open, but the district's 9-point Democratic lean gives the party a strong structural advantage. State assemblymember Jacqui Irwin has raised over $800,000 and benefits from outside support, while Republican Sam Gallucci has raised less than half as much with minimal cash on hand and no visible outside backing.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democrat around 95%. The expected margin sits in the mid-to-high teens, with the open-seat dynamic the main source of uncertainty.
